job.style: a clear textbook explanation with one worked example

passage: In geometry, an angle is formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint called the vertex. The size of an angle depends entirely on the amount of rotation between its two arms, not on the physical length of those arms. If you extend the arms of an angle, the angle measurement remains unchanged. A straight angle measures exactly 180 degrees and is considered a valid angle, even though it appears as a straight line. When using a protractor, you must place the centre mark exactly on the vertex and align the baseline with one arm to get an accurate reading. Regarding shapes, a triangle is classified as isosceles if at least two of its sides are equal in length, regardless of the length of the third side. Furthermore, all squares are special types of rectangles because they possess four right angles and opposite sides that are parallel. When identifying 3D solids, remember that edges are the straight line segments where two faces meet, and curved boundaries are not considered edges. For example, a cylinder has two circular faces and one curved surface, but it has zero straight edges. Always focus on the properties of the shape rather than its orientation or size to classify it correctly.

items.evidence: If you extend the arms of an angle, the angle measurement remains unchanged.
items.q: Meena draws a 40 degree angle and then makes both arms longer. What is the angle now?
options: Still exactly 40 degrees
More than 40 degrees
Less than 40 degrees
Exactly 80 degrees
items.explain: Extending the arms does not change the turn between them, so it stays 40 degrees.

wrong.why: thinks longer arms make the angle bigger
thinks longer arms make the opening narrower
thinks doubling arm length doubles the angle

items.evidence: A straight angle measures exactly 180 degrees and is considered a valid angle, even though it appears as a straight line.
items.q: Two rays start at one vertex and point in opposite directions. What do they make?
options: A straight angle of 180 degrees
A line, which is not an angle
A reflex angle, bigger than a right angle
A right angle of 90 degrees
items.explain: Opposite rays form a straight angle of 180 degrees, which is a valid angle.

wrong.why: thinks a straight line cannot be an angle
thinks any angle bigger than a right angle is reflex

items.evidence: When using a protractor, you must place the centre mark exactly on the vertex and align the baseline with one arm to get an accurate reading.
items.q: Rohan puts the protractor's centre mark halfway along one arm. What will happen?
options: His reading will not be accurate at all
His reading will be accurate on any arm point
His reading will be accurate if the baseline matches
His reading will grow with the arm's length
items.explain: The centre mark must sit exactly on the vertex; otherwise the reading is not accurate.

wrong.why: thinks the centre can go anywhere along an arm
thinks lining up the baseline is enough
thinks arm length changes the angle

items.evidence: Regarding shapes, a triangle is classified as isosceles if at least two of its sides are equal in length, regardless of the length of the third side.
items.q: A triangle has sides 6 cm, 6 cm and 5.9 cm. Which type is it?
options: Isosceles, because two of its sides match
Equilateral, because all sides are nearly equal
Scalene, because its third side is different
Isosceles, but only if it points upward
items.explain: Two sides are equal, so it is isosceles, whatever the third side's length.

wrong.why: thinks a nearly equal third side stops it being isosceles
thinks one different side makes it scalene
thinks orientation decides the triangle's type

items.evidence: For example, a cylinder has two circular faces and one curved surface, but it has zero straight edges.
items.q: How many edges does a cylinder have, and why?
options: Zero, because its boundaries are curved
Two, one around each circular face
Three, one for each face or surface
Four, counting the lines in its drawing
items.explain: Edges are straight segments where faces meet; a cylinder's boundaries are curved, so it has none.

wrong.why: counts every line drawn in a picture
